- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.37
- Datum: 28.7.1940
- Objekttyp: Brief

pages.transcription:
28. July 1940
Dear Hannah, we are, as I wrote to Lotte in midst
of a heat wave and had today the hottest day since
four years 1940 but we do not feel much of it as our
rooms are fairly cool and all cafeterias ice cooled. So
do not pity us. We will have a kind of winter in Brazil
As to your daughter, Lotte has written to
you what happened. Stephen Wise has spontaneously offered
us to cable his affidavit and we were sure he has done
so. Unfortunately the same day appeared in all news-
papers the notice that the action has been stopped and
affidavits were superfluous. Now when suddenly the
American Government after three weeks offers slips
it seems that affidavits will have to be given again
and we do immediately all necessary steps. You know
me and Lotte enough to know that it was not our
fault but just this day when we were proud to have
settled all appears this notice and Stephen Wise
seems to have stopped his cable as superfluous
Yesterday we were invited at Reader's Digest
and I hope to write again something only not
like the last time without the expected result. I
join an interview with the New York Times so
that you may see, that we are busy here - we see
more people than we expected and time passes
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief in violetter Tinte. Gut lesbar.

pages.transcription:
quickly. We leave the 8th of August for Brazil, all
further arrangements will be made from there, where
we arrive the 21th of August.
You may imagine with how much eagerness
we follow all the news concerning England; the interest
and sympathy here is raising from day to day and
we hope that all possible help will be given to the
last country which fights for freedom. I suppose that
you have quiet days at Bath, sometimes we wish
to be there with you all, sometimes we wish to have
you all with you here. But I hope from all my heart
that we will be together soon. Love to all and
kindest regards from yours
Stefan Zweig
The interview from New York Times please to keep for our
records
Dear Hanna, I am still hoping to
get news from you while we are here,
and would be glad to hear that Man-
fred as well as Levinthals are with
you. I was very much upset that against
his assurances the affidavit had not
been cabled, but I hope to settle this on
Monday and will then send you a cable. Lotte
